newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares swing to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares swing to new record close.

text.p: Dutch blue chips picked up in the final hour of trade on Tuesday to set a new record closing high, cheered by buoyant bonds and a strong Wall Street start.
The AEX index of leading shares closed the session up 1.69 points at a new all-time high of 589.15, fractionally back from a fresh intra-day high of 589.57.
Dealers said the rise had been backed by reasonable trading volumes, but that overall sentiment was mixed.
Index heavyweight Royal Dutch had provided major support with a gain of 4.50 guilders to 283.40 after early profit-taking, they said.
By contrast Unilever had undermined the index, dipping 1.30 to 271.40 as investors took profits.
Publisher VNU also posted losses, falling 60 cents to close at 32.90 guilders after it announced it had acquired a 14.99 percent stake in British exhibitions organisor Blenheim.
Prior to the announcement the stock had been trading down 30 cents in a generally lower market. Shortly after the news was released VNU shares were trading down one guilder at 32.50.
VNU said the buy was a long-term investment in line with its strategy of expanding its range of activities and geographic spread, but dealers said the market remained unconvinced.
"Frankly speaking, we don't know precisely what VNU wants with this stake," one said.
Early trade was dominated by private investors and most activity was focussed on the AMX index of midcap stocks.
Major gainers included technical wholesaler Otra, which jumped 1.80 guilders to 32.90 on a broker's Buy recommendation following indications its German activities were picking up.

Builder NBM Amstelland also added 80 cents to 34.0 guilders after it said it expected a 10-15 percent growth in earnings per share after 1996. "It's not really news, but people are seizing on any excuse to buy," a dealer said.

Dutch retail and business services group Vendex closed 0.70 guilders higher at 72.50 after announcing it planned to sell off its 36 percent stake in department store chain Koninklijke Bijenkorf Beheer.

Vendex said it was spinning off KBB because it was no longer considered a strategic investment. A spokesman said Vendex had held the KBB stake since the 1970s with the aim of forging a strategic alliance at some point, but that KBB had indicated this was unlikely in the foreseeable future.
Dealers said Vendex was being driven higher by speculation it would use the KBB proceeds to finance an imminent takeover.
Possible candidates mentioned included French business services group BIS and U.S. temporary employment group Kelly.

"There has been an awful lot of buy interest for Vendex on the strength of this news, but there's also one big seller in the market, so on balance the share price rise has been capped," one dealer said.
Vendex said later the KBB proceeds had not been earmarked for a near-term acquisition.
KBB itself lost heavily on the news, shedding 6.10 guilders to 140.10. "It's a bad sign that Vendex seems to have lost confidence in the stock," a dealer said.
